problemSignature.pattern: two two-terminal footprints placed collinearly with target-net pads separated by unrelated pads
problemSignature.example: R8/D1 pads ordered LED_PWR_RET, GND, +3V3, LED_PWR_RET
problemSignature.symptom: exact finisher can reduce unconnected only by adding DRC violations or shorts

rootCause: The placement engine allowed a two-component chain to interleave unrelated nets between the two pads that must connect. The router then needed vias or long detours around adjacent pads/tracks for what should have been a simple local series connection.
fixSummary: Detect interleaved two-terminal chains during routeability scoring and penalize or repair placement before routing. Recommended action is to rotate or stagger the two-terminal pair before FreeRouting/exact finishing.

testsAdded: routeability optimizer detects interleaved two-terminal chains before routing
routeability scoring penalizes known placement blockers

conditions: two-terminal footprints share a row or column
same-net endpoint pads are separated by unrelated-net pads
local exact routing repeatedly creates clearance, crossing, or short regressions

recipe: Extract two-terminal pad positions before routing.
Detect repeated target-net pads separated by unrelated-net pads across two refs.
Penalize the placement candidate and prefer rotation/staggering before route export.
If discovered post-route, classify as placement repair rather than continuing random exact-route attempts.
safetyRules: Do not change footprints, packages, symbols, nets, or pads.
Do not use blind, buried, micro, or via-in-pad repairs.
Only promote placement repair after DRC/ERC and connectivity improve.

after.engineImprovement: routeability detector added before routing/placement promotion
